name: Hyoid / neck posture meta

lead: The hyoid meta is the belief that a low hyoid bone, forward neck posture and submental fat blunt the angle between chin and neck. People work on it for a sharper under-chin line and a cleaner jawline in profile.

The hyoid is a horseshoe-shaped bone in the front of the neck, held by muscles and ligaments. Medical literature on its position concerns breathing and swallowing, and a lower hyoid is associated with obstructive sleep apnea. No study has tested whether exercises move the hyoid or change neck contour.

paras: Users combine chin tucks, neck and posture exercises and tongue posture with fat loss to reduce under-chin fullness, and check results in profile photos. Some also discuss submental injections or liposuction.
No harms are documented for the exercises themselves in the sources reviewed. Related procedures such as submental injections or liposuction are medical interventions with their own risks.

angle.text: The goal is a sharper chin-to-neck angle and cleaner profile through neck posture work, chin tucks and reducing under-chin fat. Hyoid research concerns airway anatomy, so the link to appearance comes from forum theory.

lead: The hyoid or neck posture meta is a set of beliefs in looksmaxxing communities that the position of the hyoid bone, together with neck posture and submental fat, determines the sharpness of the jawline and neck in profile. Users describe a "low" or "bad" hyoid as flattening the angle between chin and neck, and they discuss ways to "raise" it.

The hyoid is a horseshoe-shaped bone in the front of the neck, between the chin and the thyroid cartilage, held in place by muscles and ligaments rather than by joints with other bones [1]. Medical literature on its position concerns breathing and swallowing rather than appearance: a lower hyoid is associated with obstructive sleep apnea [1][2]. No published study that the wiki has located has tested whether exercises or posture change the visible neck contour by moving the hyoid in healthy people.

paras: The hyoid sits in the midline of the neck, between the base of the mandible and the third cervical vertebra at rest, and is described as loosely tied to the skeleton through muscles and ligaments [1]. Muscles of the tongue, floor of the mouth, larynx and pharynx attach to it. It supports breathing, swallowing and speech and helps keep the upper airway open during sleep [1].

Reference sources on the hyoid do not discuss how it shapes the external neck or jawline [1]. In looksmaxxing discussion, the visible neck contour is attributed both to bone position and to soft tissue such as submental fat, which some forum users distinguish explicitly from "hyoid" [3].

No studies found on hyoid position and facial or neck appearance in the general population. Related clinical research is on the airway. A meta-analysis of cephalometric studies found that adults with obstructive sleep apnea had a hyoid positioned lower and further from reference landmarks than people without the condition [2]. A 2025 pilot trial of web-based orofacial myofunctional therapy in adults with sleep apnea reported improved hyoid position after 12 weeks; the study did not test mewing, according to a description of it [4]. A 2025 meta-analysis of airway ultrasound examined measurements such as tongue thickness and skin-to-epiglottis distance in predicting difficult airways, not appearance [5].

On looksmax.org, the hyoid is a frequent topic, with thread titles asking how to raise, improve or fix it. Users describe a low hyoid as disrupting the side profile and ask whether chin tucks and neck curls change it, with some replies expressing doubt [3]. Submental fat reduction through surgery or injected fat-dissolving products is also discussed in those threads. This article does not reproduce procedural details.

Anatomy references and the airway literature treat hyoid position as a marker of upper-airway anatomy, and hyoid suspension is a surgical procedure used in sleep apnea [1]. Mainstream orthodontic organizations, as summarized in one encyclopedia, state that there is no credible evidence that tongue-posture practices such as mewing reshape the face or jaw [4].

lore.intro: The hyoid is discussed on looksmax.org mainly as a presumed determinant of side-profile neck definition, often alongside submental fat and neck posture [3].
